queries.query: transformer architectures for medical image segmentation
queries.ground_truth: Transformer-based architectures such as Vision Transformers and hybrid CNN-Transformer models have been applied to medical image segmentation tasks, improving accuracy on datasets like CT and MRI scans compared to purely convolutional approaches.

queries.query: federated learning for clinical data privacy
queries.ground_truth: Federated learning allows training machine learning models across decentralized clinical datasets without sharing raw patient data, preserving privacy while enabling collaborative model improvement across institutions.

queries.query: large language models for biomedical named entity recognition
queries.ground_truth: Large language models fine-tuned on biomedical corpora such as PubMed have shown strong performance on named entity recognition tasks, identifying entities like diseases, genes, and drugs from clinical and scientific text.

queries.query: graph neural networks for drug-target interaction prediction
queries.ground_truth: Graph neural networks model drug and protein structures as graphs and learn interaction patterns, achieving competitive performance on drug-target interaction prediction benchmarks compared to traditional machine learning methods.

queries.query: attention mechanisms for protein structure prediction
queries.ground_truth: Attention mechanisms, particularly as used in transformer models like AlphaFold, have significantly advanced protein structure prediction by capturing long-range dependencies between amino acid residues.

queries.query: aprendizaje automático para clasificación de texto clínico
queries.ground_truth: Machine learning models including SVMs, CNNs, and transformer-based models have been applied to clinical text classification tasks such as ICD coding, discharge summary categorization, and clinical note triage.

Deep learning has been applied across multiple healthcare domains including medical image analysis, clinical NLP, drug discovery, and patient outcome prediction, with varying levels of clinical adoption.
